style_reference.content: Original forest game scenery only. No lobby UI or previous console artwork was provided as a design reference.

generation_brief: A fresh woodland pixel-art handheld console, with sculpted tree trunks and roots, worn heartwood, sparse moss and leaves, varied irregular silhouettes and quiet areas. A thin border around a black game display, a connected two-direction wooden rocker, an irregular rabbit button and two small utility keys. No MOVE or JUMP captions, repeating wood tiles, generic rectangular controls or padded screen shadow. All final artwork is rasterized to one native pixel grid.
runtime_composition: The menu and game share the original 400x256 aspect ratio. A continuous wood material is copied at 1:1 onto the frame canvas; unusually large surfaces extend it by reflection. The old body plates are retained as source artwork and are not used at runtime. Control sprites are masked from the original illustrations, with proportional smaller variants prepared once. The chosen native sprite and its lettering are copied at integer coordinates without enlargement. Only the completed frame canvas is enlarged, with one shared integer number of physical pixels per artwork pixel, capped at two CSS pixels to keep utility labels legible on tablets.

assets.final_prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: a production pixel-art wood material sheet for a responsive woodland game controller UI. The provided image is STYLE AND PALETTE REFERENCE ONLY, not an edit target and not a layout to reproduce. Generate a brand-new square 1024x1024 image that is completely filled edge-to-edge with continuous warm carved heartwood, cinnamon-orange and dark umber grain, occasional small swirling knots, and sparse intertwined narrow roots with tiny olive-green leaf clusters. Match the reference's classic richly shaded 1990s woodland pixel-art feeling, but use a single consistent fine pixel grid everywhere. The whole image is usable material: NO black screen, NO opening, NO frame silhouette, NO buttons, NO lettering, NO logo, NO interface, NO perspective, NO empty or transparent regions. Straight-on flat orthographic material plane, even warm light from upper left, restrained local shading, no large central focal object or huge tree rings. Varied medium and small grain, generous quiet wood patches between details, roots and leaves scattered sparsely so arbitrary narrow strips and broad rectangles look natural when cropped. Pixel-art colors with crisp square pixel detail; no pre-enlarged pixel blocks, no mixed pixel sizes, no blurry regions, no photographic realism. This texture will be uniformly reduced once into one 512x512 native sprite sheet and then copied at 1:1 into every UI panel, without stretching. Make all local details equally fine across the entire image.
assets.preparation: Uniform nearest-neighbor reduction to 512x512; 96-color palette without dithering. Top, bottom and side panels are crops from this single native material.

assets.final_edit_prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit target: this portrait wooden pixel-art game console. Change ONLY the rabbit-shaped engraving on the jump button at the right. Replace that rabbit cavity with ONE simple UPWARD-POINTING TRIANGLE, with no shaft, stem, chevron or extra marks. The triangle must be exactly the same shape and treatment as the existing left/right triangular engravings on the joined rocker: imagine duplicating the rocker's right-facing triangle and rotating it 90 degrees counterclockwise. Same proportions, same dark brown recessed cavity, same thin carved wood edge, same pixel-art surface shading. Place it at the optical center of the jump button's front cut-wood face. Keep the irregular jump button's outer silhouette, wood rings, perspective and material exactly as they are. Preserve all other controls, all other pixels, the two blank utility buttons, blank top bridge, foliage, roots, pure-black screen opening and framing. Do not add text, logos, rabbits or new decorations. Same aspect ratio and colors.
assets.preparation: Nearest-neighbor reduction to the native raster; 96-color palette without dithering. Used as the portrait control sprite source; lettering is drawn on the final native grid.

original_logo.preparation: Original letter faces are used as a native-resolution carving stencil. The original blue extrusion and green shadow are excluded. The runtime shades the actual underlying wood pixels into charred grooves, a recessed lower wall, and a narrow lit upper lip; no translucent logo overlay is used.
original_logo.placement: 55 native pixels wide, centered in the top wood strip only when the layout leaves enough room for it. No extra margin is reserved for the logo.

utility_lettering.appearance: Dark, grain-textured carving with a warm highlight immediately above the letters. Labels match the optical center and tilt of each wood face. Adjacent source stroke pixels are reconnected after rotation, preserving four separate, continuous letters for both Back and Full.
